notes: Version 2.0 is a status correction. It withdraws the Level 1 theorem of version 1 (no dimensional parameter independent of the Born–Infeld constant c_BI can enter the admissibility constraints), its corollary on fields with independent dimensional couplings, and the application to Reissner–Nordström and Schwarzschild–de Sitter exteriors. The proof rested on premises that the cited papers do not contain: a power law for the pair capacity (O24 states none), a continuum limit (Q5a proves convergence of the admissibility form to the zero form and leaves the spatial limit open), a requirement of equal admissibility weights on a fibre (ENI states none), and Foundation axioms A3 and A4 fixing a unique primitive scale (A3 is non-premature selection, A4 projection locking). Its three cases also have internal gaps: a depth-dependent factor need not change a power-law exponent, a configuration weight does not make the projection injective, and the case split was not exhaustive; the Reissner–Nordström / Schwarzschild–de Sitter application was internally inconsistent. The failure of the proof does not show that every Level 1 property is false; the question is recorded as open, with no conditional theorem in its place. The version keeps dimensional observations: the model does not fix the physical dimension of c_BI, a gap recorded rather than filled; the definition of an independent dimensional parameter is stated relative to a supplied dimensional assignment; under such an assignment, a constant factor depending only on a parameter whose dimension lies outside the span of the bound's ingredients is constant, and a dimensionless factor rescales c_BI (corrected from a square root in version 1). The Level 1 / Level 2 distinction is kept, both levels open. The statement that the Gram rigidity classification is derived under the Born–Infeld bound is withdrawn: that classification is character-theoretic and scale-free. The attribution to Q6b of a Schwarzschild uniqueness result is removed. The version adds a labelled interpretation, a conclusion, primary references on dimensional analysis (Buckingham; Bridgman), refreshed bibliography titles, and a font and Unicode-extraction preamble.
